subject: TrialHealth — MAP: POC connectivity sprint (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alexis Howard <alexis@trialhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@trialhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TrialHealth — MAP: POC connectivity sprint (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Hi Alexis / Samir —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion, I’ve sketched a compact MAP to get TrialHealth into a productionlike POC environment so we can validate latency and cost at scale. The items below are the minimums we need in the evaluation MAP to unblock the integration team and begin test traffic.

POC MAP (high level) — target close: 4 weeks from kickoff
- Org & tenant creation: create TrialHealth org in Redwood console, assign SSO / SAML owner
- API keys: provision a service account + ephemeral API key flow for dev/staging; rotate schedule noted
- IP allowlist: provide public egress CIDRs we should allow; Redwood to provide egress IP set for hosted endpoints
- VPC peering / private endpoint: establish peering connection (optional initial sprint; required for HIPAA lane)

Proposed milestone cadence (example):
1) Kickoff + SOC2 and procurement ask (Day 0)
2) Org & API keys provisioned (Day 3–5)
3) IP allowlist test and connectivity smoke (Day 7–10)
4) VPC peering setup & end-to-end sample inference run (Day 14–21)

Can you confirm the internal contacts on your side (network, security, procurement) and whether procurement needs a full quote ahead of org creation? I’ve attached a one-page task list (Proposed_MAP_Tasklist.xlsx) and the network requirements doc (Network_Requirements.pdf) that our infra team will use.

Next steps I propose:
- Please confirm stakeholders and the preferred kickoff window (next Tue/Thu morning PT)
- If peering is required, indicate whether TrialHealth prefers a cloud-to-cloud peering (AWS VPC peering) or transit/VPN setup — we’ll loop in our infra engineers accordingly

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

Attachments: Proposed_MAP_Tasklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), Network_Requirements.pdf (PDF)

From: Alexis Howard <alexis@trialhealth.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@trialhealth.com>, Lisa Grant <lisa.grant@trialhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TrialHealth — MAP: POC connectivity sprint (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Ben —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Internal contacts: Security = Samir (copied), Network = Rajesh Kaur (I’ll intro separately), Procurement = Lisa Grant (copied).
- Procurement: they want a basic statement of work + estimated monthly cost before approving org creation. Lisa, do you want a draft quote?
- Peering: we prefer VPC peering in AWS for the initial POC to reduce NAT complexity; we will provide our VPC CIDR and a couple of contact windows for peering maintenance (normally Tue/Wed 02:00–06:00 UTC).
- Keys: we will need an ephemeral key flow for testing and documentation on key rotation. Also, please confirm whether Redwood can support an allowlist for a set of static egress IPs for test traffic.

I’ve attached our network safety doc for your infra team to review (TrialHealth_Internal_Network_Safety.docx).

If you can get the draft SOW/quote and the expected IP ranges from Redwood by Monday EOD PT, we’ll push procurement to sign off this week.

—Alexis
Alexis Howard | Dir. of Integrations
TrialHealth
alexis@trialhealth.com

Attachments: TrialHealth_Internal_Network_Safety.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TrialHealth — MAP: POC connectivity sprint (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)

Alexis — thanks for the quick turn. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and proposing a slightly tighter plan so procurement can get a quote and we can start keys/org work immediately.

Updated, condensed timeline (aiming for 2-week rapid POC if procurement signs promptly):
- Day 0 (kickoff): confirm SOW scope and procurement approvals; SOW draft delivered by Redwood sales
- Day 1–2: Redwood creates TrialHealth org and a service account; we stage ephemeral API key flow and share initial key rotation docs
- Day 3–6: Exchange IP ranges; Redwood provides static egress IP set for hosted endpoints; TrialHealth applies allowlist and runs connectivity smoke
- Day 7–10: VPC peering window (if agreed): agree on peering window (we can accommodate Tue/Wed 02:00–06:00 UTC) and exchange route tables/cidrs
- Day 11–14: End-to-end test: sample inference runs + perf capture; capture token-level cost and latency metrics for your evaluation

Marissa — can you own the peering coordination and provide the engineering contact on Redwood’s networking side? I’ll prepare a short SOW and estimate for Lisa.

Alexis/Lisa — I’ll aim to send the SOW draft and an estimated monthly run-rate by Monday 09:00 PT. Ben

Thanks Ben — I’ll take point on peering coordination and routing. Diego (copied) from Infra will be the technical owner for the peering work and will coordinate with Rajesh on TrialHealth’s side. Diego — can you confirm the preflight checklist below and whether we need any additional info from TrialHealth before we schedule the peering window?

Redwood preflight for VPC peering (short checklist):
- Shared VPC CIDR blocks and desired route table entries
- Peering request (we’ll initiate from our AWS account) and acceptance window
- Security groups / NACL considerations for control-plane endpoints
- Expected traffic pattern and sample test key for smoke runs

Operational notes:
- For the ephemeral API keys we plan to provision a service account (dev/stage) and provide rotation docs; production keys can be scoped separately after the POC.
- I’ll also post a short runbook to the shared Drive folder for the connectivity window and attach the runbook here (peering_runbook_v1.md).

Alexis/Lisa — we should be able to meet the Monday SOW timeline Ben mentioned. If procurement needs additional terms (data retention, audit logs) list them and I’ll add to the SOW.

Regards,
Marissa Cole | Head of Customer Success (POC Delivery)
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
